proposals.title: Write required ADRs for DEFINIR items blocking packages/core
proposals.why_now: ADR-002 requires the hash function to be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before rand() is implemented. ADR-009 requires its own ADR before CanonicalEncoder is written. ADR-004 requires the enforcement mechanism for explicit rounding modes to be decided before arithmetic helpers are written. All three are explicitly marked DEFINIR in the spec, and §19 mandates an ADR before implementation. Writing these ADRs is the minimal unlocking action for packages/core — without them any implementation of rand(), CanonicalEncoder, or division helpers violates the spec's own process rules and may require breaking changes to encodingVersion later.

proposals.title: packages/core — branded numeric types, positional RNG, CanonicalEncoder, arithmetic helpers
proposals.why_now: Every other package imports core. The branded types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate as bigint; Tick and index types as safe-integer number) are the compiler-enforced mechanism for ADR-003 and ADR-004 — without them downstream packages will use plain number and the type-level invariant system collapses. The positional rand() is the root of all determinism. The CanonicalEncoder must exist before any StateHash is produced; ADR-009 explicitly requires it be implemented before any hash of state exists. This is the single highest-leverage implementation task in FASE-1.

proposals.title: packages/world — price generator with two noise layers and two assets
proposals.why_now: The price generator is the load-bearing structure of the whole simulation. INV-02 — direct price query equals tick-by-tick accumulation — is explicitly described in the spec as the most important test in the project. Getting positional O(1) price query wrong retroactively invalidates all determinism guarantees. Implementing with two assets and two octaves (as scoped in FASE-1) yields the first falsifiable determinism test and establishes the fixed-point arithmetic patterns all later world computation inherits. The performance baseline frozen by tools/bench also depends on this module existing.

proposals.title: packages/domain — double-entry ledger and spot market order
proposals.why_now: The ledger and order execution layer is the other major FASE-1 prerequisite alongside the price generator. INV-04 through INV-07 (transaction balance per commodity, zero-sum BRL, zero-sum per asset, rounding residue) must be green for FASE-1 acceptance. These invariants are easiest to establish now while the ledger is small and before derivatives and the full tick loop add complexity. The ledger can be implemented in parallel with packages/world since both depend only on packages/core.

warnings: The hash function for rand() is a DEFINIR item (ADR-002) that must be specified bit-exactly in an ADR before any implementation of rand() is written. Any change to the hash function after world-state hashes exist requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes. This ADR must precede packages/core implementation.

The technical enforcement mechanism for explicit rounding modes is a DEFINIR item (ADR-004). An ADR must specify how calling division without an explicit mode becomes a compile error or blocking lint error before arithmetic helpers in packages/core are written. Implementing the helpers before this ADR exists violates §19 and may require breaking API changes.

The price generator in §5.1 constructs prices in log-space, which requires log and exp. Both are prohibited in pure packages by §13. A fixed-point or lookup-table implementation must be specified in an ADR before packages/world work begins — otherwise the price generator violates either §13 or the cross-platform determinism requirement of INV-19. This ADR is not explicitly listed in the spec's known gaps but is a necessary consequence of §5.1 and §13 together.

The octave count, block periods, and amplitude parameters for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are DEFINIR (§5.1). These must be recorded in a versioned config file before the price generator is implemented, because changing any parameter after the performance baseline is frozen in FASE-1 requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates reference StateHashes.

FASE-1 acceptance requires a minimum Electron installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI. The spec states this explicitly to surface ABI and packaging issues early. Deferring the Electron shell beyond FASE-1 is prohibited by the spec (§14.6): 'Instalador que abre uma janela vazia na FASE-1 vale mais que instalador perfeito na FASE-7.'
